dynamicGatewayObservation.summary: The desktop supervisor allocated four distinct dynamic loopback ports for the gateway and three MCP services. Every service became healthy, the gateway health probe returned 200, a tokenless protected request returned 403, the fixed development gateway port remained closed, and signup traffic reached the dynamic gateway. The two first-party apps used distinct authenticated random loopback processes; uninstall and restart observations showed no cross-app process or lifecycle leakage.

cleanup: Every launch and restart was stopped by the recorded task-owned launcher PID and descendant tree. All observed gateway, MCP, Vite, app-runtime, and app ports closed; the final desktop and Resume app PIDs stopped; no new WebView2 process remained; the owner's checkout stayed clean at its original branch and revision; and only the task-owned clone, bundle, application data, temp files, logs, screenshots, and synthetic credential were removed.
